about: The adjudication layer of the Leonida Ledger v4: every dispute between the 22 sources in trophies.json, shown two-sided with this guide's call; the at-risk register; the open questions; the roadmap's editorial decisions; the 100% completion ledger; per-source claim counts and the coverage matrix. Counts in the claim and coverage tables are computed from trophies.json itself.

disputes.topic: How long is the platinum, really?

a.claim: PowerPyx's roadmap estimates 150–200 hours for the platinum, assuming story-first play and no wasted cleanup.

b.claim: KeenGamer's roadmap estimates 220–260 hours, counting full collectible sweeps and the 100% tail at first-timer pace.

disputes.call: Plan 200 hours. The gap is mostly pace assumptions, not content: PowerPyx prices a guided run, KeenGamer prices an unguided one. HowLongToBeat's early completionist reports sit between the two, closer to 200. The hero dashboard's time-remaining estimate uses 200.

disputes.topic: How hard is the platinum?

a.claim: PowerPyx rates the platinum 3/10 difficulty — nothing is skill-gated beyond the range golds.

b.claim: PSNProfiles' community difficulty vote sits nearer 5/10, driven by The Shootist's 42 gold medals and the 250-stunt grind.

disputes.call: 4/10. There is no hard trophy in the list, but two long accuracy/endurance grinds (range golds, stunts) punish rushing. Difficulty here is stamina, not skill — plan sessions accordingly.

disputes.topic: Meditation spots: 18 or 15?

a.claim: Exophase's tracked list and most guides count 18 meditation spots — the number the trophy itself tracks.

b.claim: GTABase's 100% checklist counts 15, folding three rooftop spots into their districts rather than listing them separately.

disputes.call: 18. The trophy's own counter is the authority for the trophy; the 15-count is a checklist presentation choice. This tracker counts 18 and the three rooftop spots are named in the guide.

disputes.topic: Does the Chapter 1 balcony meditation close?

a.claim: PowerPyx warns the Ocean Beach balcony spot may become unreachable when Chapter 1 ends — making Positive Mental Attitude the list's one missable.

b.claim: OutputLag reports every meditation spot still reachable after the story, balcony included.

disputes.call: Treat it as missable. The safe play costs two minutes in Chapter 1; the cost of the other side being wrong is a second playthrough. Asymmetric stakes decide this one — meditate on the balcony in Chapter 1.

disputes.topic: Is anything in this list truly missable?

a.claim: KeenGamer counts exactly 1 possibly missable trophy (Positive Mental Attitude, via the balcony spot).

b.claim: OutputLag counts 0 missables, since it reports the balcony spot reachable post-story.

disputes.call: 1 possibly missable, 2 watch items. The count follows D-04: until the balcony question is settled by more than assertion, the honest label is 'possibly', and the guide flags it everywhere it matters.

disputes.topic: Activity types: 9 or 10?

a.claim: The official list's tracking and most guides say 9 activity types for Master of None.

b.claim: eGamers counts 10, splitting drone racing from road racing as its own type.

disputes.call: 9 — the official tracking wins. If you have sampled all 9 and the trophy is silent, one extra drone race resolves it either way; the guide's steps say exactly that.

disputes.topic: Shooting Range challenges: 42 or 40?

a.claim: PowerPyx and the official list count 42 range challenges, all gold-medal targets for The Shootist.

b.claim: KeenGamer's index shows 40 standard challenges, treating the last 2 as unlockable bonus lanes that open after the story.

disputes.call: 42, with the unlock caveat printed in the guide: if your board shows 40, finish the story and the final pair appears. Both sources are describing the same board at different story states.

disputes.topic: WAiNK locations: 100 mapped or 96 + 4 rumoured?

a.claim: KeenGamer's route maps exactly 100 WAiNK locations, matching the trophy's target.

b.claim: GTA Vibes' map lists 96 confirmed spots plus 4 marked 'rumoured'.

disputes.call: 100 exist. The 4 'rumoured' spots are real but sit inside interiors that open after story beats, which is why early maps missed them. If you stall at 96–99, the guide points at those interiors.

disputes.topic: Areas of Leonida: 52 or 49?

a.claim: PSNProfiles' tracking and most guides work to 52 named areas for The Goodtime State.

b.claim: GTABase counts 49, treating three island settlements in the Keys as part of their neighbouring areas.

disputes.call: 52. The trophy's banner count is the authority; if your map looks complete and the trophy is quiet, the three Keys settlements are the usual gap — the guide names the pattern.

disputes.topic: Is there really a 500-choice counter?

a.claim: Exophase reports PSN tracking 'choices made' to 500 for Actions Speak Louder.

b.claim: GTABase's 100% checklist omits any choices category, treating choices as uncounted story flavour.

disputes.call: Choices are counted and 500 is the line — two list sources and the kit's starter guide agree against one checklist's silence. If yours pops earlier, the checklist was right and nothing is lost.

disputes.topic: Story length: how long is the campaign?

a.claim: HowLongToBeat's early main-story reports cluster around 38–45 hours.

b.claim: GameSpot's coverage puts a thorough first campaign at 50+ hours once strand and activity detours are included.

disputes.call: Plan ~45 hours for the story block of the roadmap. The two numbers measure different play styles; the roadmap's stage order assumes you bank counters during the campaign, which lands between them.

disputes.topic: Does 100% require literally everything?

a.claim: PowerPyx's reading: the completion counter is weighted — some categories (e.g. every vehicle model) contribute without being fully exhausted.

b.claim: KeenGamer's reading: 100% means every tracked category at its full target, collectibles included.

disputes.call: We plan for the stricter reading — full targets everywhere (that is the 100% ledger below). If the counter is weighted after all, you finish early; planning to the looser reading and being wrong costs a second sweep of the whole map.

disputes.topic: Stunts: do repeats count toward 250?

a.claim: PowerPyx: repeat jumps still count toward Cunning Stunts' 250, just at lower value than first-time unique jumps.

b.claim: GTA-Zone's notes imply only distinct stunt events advance the counter.

disputes.call: Repeats count. The counter is a stunt total, not a unique-jump total — but unique routes are still the fast way, so the guide routes you across fresh ramps instead of farming one.

disputes.topic: Do drone race wins count toward the 20 races?

a.claim: OutputLag counts Top Fun drone wins toward Earn Cash, Not Kudos's 20 different races.

b.claim: eGamers' notes read the 20 as road and boat races only.

disputes.call: Drone wins count — the counter is 'different races', and Top Fun events are races in the game's own event classes. Winning all 14 drone locations leaves only 6 road or boat wins, as the guide lays out.

disputes.topic: Card sets: how many cards in the full run?

a.claim: KeenGamer counts 5 themed sets totalling 54 individual cards.

b.claim: GTA Vibes' collectible map shows 6 set frames, suggesting a sixth set and roughly 60 cards.

disputes.call: 5 sets, 54 cards. The sixth 'frame' on the map is the completion display case, not a set — no card in any source's list belongs to it. The trophy needs any 3 sets; the 100% ledger counts all 54 cards.

disputes.topic: How big is the vehicle catalogue?

a.claim: GTABase's vehicle database lists 186 distinct models across cars, bikes, boats and aircraft.

b.claim: eGamers' trophy notes speak of 'around 150' vehicles.

disputes.call: 186 models in the full catalogue; the trophy needs any 100 discoveries. The bigger number matters for 100% planning, not for Whip It Good itself — the guide's dealership-and-marina tour route is built on the full list.

disputes.topic: Stranger strands: how many exist?

a.claim: OutputLag counts 14 stranger strands in total across Leonida.

b.claim: GTA-Zone's list shows 12 strands, folding two short chains into their neighbours.

disputes.call: 14. Strangers & Freaks needs any 8 completed strands; A Long Road wants them all. The two disputed chains are short, late-opening strands — the guide's full-map sweep advice exists because of them.

disputes.topic: One playthrough, or two endings?

a.claim: PowerPyx: a single playthrough earns everything; no ending variation locks a trophy.

b.claim: PlayStationTrophies' roadmap thread debates whether both finale variations must be seen for full completion credit.

disputes.call: One playthrough. No source names a trophy gated behind an ending, and the finale trophy's own steps confirm variations change nothing. Keep a pre-finale save anyway — it is free insurance, not a requirement.

disputes.topic: Is there mission replay or chapter select?

a.claim: PSNProfiles' threads report no mission-replay menu found in the release build.

b.claim: Community megathread reports claim a chapter-select appears after the credits in some builds.

disputes.call: Unresolved — plan as if there is no replay. Nothing in this list needs it (the one missable risk is handled in Chapter 1), so the guide's order never depends on replay existing. Listed again as open question U-05.

disputes.topic: Are there any online trophies?

a.claim: Exophase's list shows all 55 trophies earnable in the single-player game; none references an online mode.

b.claim: RockstarINTEL's list-reveal coverage notes the publisher has not commented on a possible online tie-in.

disputes.call: No online trophies in this list. The official 55 are all single-player; if a future online mode adds its own list, it will be a separate list and a separate guide.

disputes.topic: Laundering: gross washed or net received?

a.claim: PowerPyx: Dime on the Dollar's counter tracks the gross value of marked bills put through the wash.

b.claim: eGamers' notes suggest the counter tracks the clean amount returned after the contacts' cut.

disputes.call: Gross. The description says 'earn $250,000 laundering' — the earning event is the wash, and the counter widget in this guide tracks gross thousands put through, matching the faster of the two readings being the safe plan either way.

disputes.topic: Does property spending count toward Treat Yo Self?

a.claim: OutputLag reads '$100,000 across all shops' strictly — shop purchases only; garage purchases belong to Little Boxes.

b.claim: GTA Vibes counts property-adjacent spending (fittings, services) toward the total as well.

disputes.call: Both readings converge in practice: buy the garages for Little Boxes regardless, and let shop spending — which includes fittings and services — carry Treat Yo Self. Nobody needs to farm this counter either way.

disputes.topic: Bank vaults: five branches or nine?

a.claim: PowerPyx's Maximum Withdrawal guide works with the five most accessible bank branches.

b.claim: GTABase's map marks nine bank branches with rob-able vaults.

disputes.call: Nine branches exist; the trophy needs any five robbed and escaped. The guide says vary branches rather than waiting on one to reset — with nine on the map, that is always possible.

disputes.topic: Gangs: nine, or a hidden tenth?

a.claim: The official tracking for Pest Control counts 9 gangs.

b.claim: Community reports speculate about a tenth, unmarked gang in the northern counties.

disputes.call: 9. The trophy's own counter is the requirement; if a tenth gang exists, robbing its operation is bonus income, not a requirement. No guide time should be spent hunting it for this trophy.

disputes.topic: Fishing challenges: total weight or biggest fish?

a.claim: OutputLag's detailed account: Cal's challenges are timed total-weight contests.

b.claim: GTA Vibes' shorter note describes winning by landing the round's biggest single fish.

disputes.call: Total weight — the detailed account is also the one whose other claims check out against the official description. The guide's strategy (bank small fish fast) follows the weight reading; it also happens to be decent play under the other reading.

disputes.topic: Bowling follow-through: every throw or one throw?

a.claim: eGamers reads Let's Go Bowling as a style requirement across a full game — follow-through held on every throw.

b.claim: GTABase's note suggests a single held follow-through in any game at the alley suffices.

disputes.call: Hold it on every throw of one game. It costs nothing extra, satisfies both readings, and the guide's troubleshooting step (hold from release until the ball passes the arrows) covers the timing either way.

disputes.topic: Sneakthief: what counts as 'detected'?

a.claim: OutputLag: detection means a witness completing a call or an alarm tripping; a brief glimpse you interrupt is survivable.

b.claim: KeenGamer's stricter reading: any staff member spotting you voids the clean run.

disputes.call: Play to the stricter reading (stay unseen entirely, rear entrance, night), because it satisfies both. The guide's steps are written that way; the looser reading is noted so a brief glimpse doesn't make you abandon a run that may still count.

disputes.topic: Challenging Tank: what is the trigger?

a.claim: PSNProfiles' theory thread leans toward surviving a military response involving a Rhino and escaping.

b.claim: GTA Vibes' notes lean toward simply stealing and driving a Rhino.

disputes.call: UNRESOLVED — and the case stays open on purpose. Three theories are ranked in the guide (drive it, survive-and-escape, destroy it) with a cheap test order. Anyone claiming certainty today is guessing; see U-01.

disputes.topic: Personal Best: fame milestone or partner streak?

a.claim: PSNProfiles' theory: a follower/fame milestone for the pair — 'mass appeal' read literally.

b.claim: eGamers' theory: a streak of activities completed together as a partnership.

disputes.call: UNRESOLVED. The fame reading fits the wording better, so the guide tests it first — but both theories are cheap to probe during ordinary co-op play, and neither can be missed. See U-02.

disputes.topic: The Truth Is Out There: where is the strange event?

a.claim: PSNProfiles' theory thread points at a lights/UFO event over the northern hills at a set hour.

b.claim: GTA Vibes points at a scripted roadside oddity on the swamp roads at night.

disputes.call: UNRESOLVED. The guide's cheap experiments cover both territories in a few in-game nights. Series tradition says the event exists and is findable; nobody has published a verified trigger yet. See U-03.

disputes.topic: Bad Luck, I Guess: must the fail be a mission?

a.claim: eGamers' detailed account: any failed event — mission, challenge or activity — passed on the immediate retry triggers it.

b.claim: PSNProfiles' shorter note frames it as a story-mission fail-and-retry.

disputes.call: Any event, immediate retry. The account with the mechanic's details (including the warning that free-roam deaths don't count) is the one to follow; arranging it on a 30-second challenge is the guide's method.

disputes.topic: Ten Pin: motorcycle only, or any vehicle?

a.claim: KeenGamer's account demonstrates the melee drive-by from a motorcycle and recommends it.

b.claim: GTABase notes cars perform the same melee animation, with a tighter window.

disputes.call: Any vehicle, bike in practice. The description says 'melee drive-by', not 'motorcycle' — but the collision-versus-melee distinction is the real trap, and the bike is the reliable tool. The guide teaches the bike method.

disputes.topic: Hot Together: when must your partner be present?

a.claim: OutputLag: the partner's presence is checked at the moment the wanted level clears.

b.claim: eGamers reads it as the partner needing to be present when the fourth star is raised.

disputes.call: Keep your partner with you for the whole arc — raise and escape together. That satisfies both readings and is how the guide's steps are written; the presence-at-clear detail is kept because it explains most failed attempts.

disputes.topic: Retail Therapy: may the wanted level dip between shops?

a.claim: PowerPyx: the chain breaks only if the wanted level fully clears between robberies.

b.claim: GTA-Zone's stricter note implies dropping below two stars already endangers the chain.

disputes.call: Full clear breaks the chain; dips do not. But the practical advice is identical either way — keep moving, never hide between shops — so the guide plans the tight three-shop route and treats any dip as a warning, not a reset.

at_risk.risk: The Ocean Beach balcony meditation spot may become unreachable when Chapter 1 ends (case D-04); missing it can cost a second playthrough.
at_risk.safeguard: Meditate on the balcony during Chapter 1 — two minutes, and the dispute never matters.

at_risk.risk: Watch item: the unscheduled departure depends on knowing VCIA's service gates and apron layout, which fade from memory after Chapter 4.
at_risk.safeguard: Do it immediately after VCIA Takedown, while the mission's tour of the airport is still fresh.

at_risk.risk: Watch item: the cocktail terrace sits in Chapter 1's backyard; players who rush the chapter often never return to Ocean Beach.
at_risk.safeguard: Take the cocktail in the same Chapter 1 visit as the balcony meditation — one trip closes both.

at_risk.risk: The chain resets silently if the wanted level fully clears between shops; hiding 'to be safe' is the usual cause.
at_risk.safeguard: Scout three close shops first, keep the heat on between them, and never hide mid-chain (case D-34).

at_risk.risk: If your partner is arrested or left behind during the escape, the clear may not register (case D-33).
at_risk.safeguard: Regroup before the stars finish draining; presence is checked at the moment the level empties.

at_risk.risk: A single completed witness call or alarm voids the clean run — and a fired shot is detection by itself.
at_risk.safeguard: Rear entrance at night, staff covered, no shots; if detected, leave and retry the next in-game day.

at_risk.risk: Dying or being arrested after robbing a vault voids that vault's attempt entirely.
at_risk.safeguard: Stage the escape car at the rear before entering; armour and a stocked rifle beat a faster car.

at_risk.risk: Shooting up the truck can wreck the take, and a despawn mid-chase wastes the whole setup.
at_risk.safeguard: Block the truck with a heavy vehicle, open the rear doors with one sticky charge, grab and go.

at_risk.risk: A fifth takedown landing a split-second after Combat Focus ends does not count.
at_risk.safeguard: Use the Operation Savage Glory courtyard: five clustered enemies, full meter, no reload mid-activation.

at_risk.risk: Skipping cutscenes may skip their embedded choices, quietly slowing the 500-choice counter.
at_risk.safeguard: Let scenes play on a counter-focused run; batch-tick the widget from the in-game stats page.

at_risk.risk: The fail and the successful retry must be the same event back-to-back; wandering off between attempts can break the pairing.
at_risk.safeguard: Arrange it deliberately on a 30-second challenge: fail on purpose, retry immediately (case D-31).

at_risk.risk: Strand continuations gate on story progress and time, and markers hide under the map's activity filter — strands look lost when they are not.
at_risk.safeguard: Advance the story or sleep, check the map filter, and track completions — not starts — in the widget.

at_risk.risk: The counter stalls at 99% for most players because of one unstarted stranger strand or one small miscellaneous category.
at_risk.safeguard: Audit the completion page category by category against this ledger; the smallest categories are the usual gap.

at_risk.risk: Grinding against a 40-challenge board: the final 2 lanes only unlock after the story (case D-07).
at_risk.safeguard: If your board shows 40, finish the story first — do not burn sessions hunting lanes that do not exist yet.

at_risk.risk: Clipping a pedestrian with the wheel is a collision, not a melee hit, and does not count.
at_risk.safeguard: Motorcycle, walking pace along the boardwalk, swing as you pass — match their speed before the pass (case D-32).

at_risk.risk: Marked bills sitting in a stash earn nothing and the wash cycle takes in-game time; a stalled pipeline is how this trophy runs late.
at_risk.safeguard: Keep bills moving through contacts in parallel with other cleanup; unlock higher-tier contacts through strand work.

unconfirmed.question: Challenging Tank — what actually triggers it?
unconfirmed.status: Open. Three working theories, ranked by the guide: steal and drive a Rhino; survive a Rhino-led military response and escape; destroy a Rhino. No source has published a verified trigger. See case D-28.

unconfirmed.question: Personal Best — fame milestone or partner streak?
unconfirmed.status: Open. The wording ('a partnership with mass appeal') favours a fame/followers milestone for the pair; a partner-activity streak is the rival reading. Both are cheap to probe in ordinary co-op play. See case D-29.

unconfirmed.question: The Truth Is Out There — where and when is the strange event?
unconfirmed.status: Open. Northern-hills lights event and swamp-road oddity are the two candidate sightings; no verified time, place or trigger has been published. See case D-30.

unconfirmed.question: Will a future online mode add its own trophy list?
unconfirmed.status: Open, and out of scope for this list: the official 55 are all single-player (case D-20). Any online list would be separate and is not planned for here.

unconfirmed.question: Does mission replay or chapter select exist in the release build?
unconfirmed.status: Open. Reports conflict (case D-19). This guide never depends on replay existing: the one missable risk is handled inside Chapter 1 itself.

roadmap_decisions.call: plan 200 hours — the dashboard's time-remaining estimate uses it
treat as 4/10 — stamina, not skill; pace the two long grinds
budget ~45 hours for the campaign, banking counters as you go
one possibly missable — secure the balcony meditation in Chapter 1
track 18 — the trophy's own counter is the authority
plan to full targets everywhere — the 1,777-line ledger below
one playthrough; keep a pre-finale save as free insurance
42 — if your board shows 40, the last pair unlocks after the story
